microtheory.name: sociology
microtheory.definition: Sociology — scientific study of society, social interaction, institutions, groups, stratification. Durkheim, Weber, Marx, Mead, Goffman, Bourdieu. Macro (social structure, institutions) + meso (organizations, networks) + micro (interaction, identity). Substrate analogue: the level above individual psychology — institutions + groups + structures that constrain and enable individual behavior.

concepts.name: society
concepts.definition: Bounded population sharing institutions + culture + territory. Variable scale: tribal band to nation-state to global.

concepts.name: social_structure
concepts.definition: Stable patterns of relations + institutions shaping individual behavior. Substrate analogue: substrate's foundational Mts constraining variable runtime.

concepts.name: social_institution
concepts.definition: Established set of norms + roles around recurring social need. Family, education, religion, economy, polity. Substrate analogue: persistent multi-agent patterns.

concepts.name: norm_social
concepts.definition: Shared expectation of behavior. Folkways, mores, laws. Sanctioned by group. Substrate analogue: substrate's distributed rule-enforcement.

concepts.name: role_social
concepts.definition: Set of behaviors expected of person in particular position. Substrate analogue: substrate's context-conditioned behavior pattern.

concepts.name: durkheim_division_labor
concepts.definition: Émile Durkheim 1893. Mechanical solidarity (likeness) → organic solidarity (interdependence) as division of labor increases.

concepts.name: weber_rationalisation
concepts.definition: Max Weber. Modernity = increasing rationalisation, bureaucratisation, disenchantment. Protestant Ethic + Spirit of Capitalism.

concepts.name: marx_class_conflict
concepts.definition: Karl Marx. History driven by class struggle. Modes of production shape consciousness. Bourgeoisie vs proletariat under capitalism.

concepts.name: mead_symbolic_interaction
concepts.definition: George Herbert Mead. Self emerges through symbolic interaction. 'I' vs 'me'. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity through interaction.

concepts.name: goffman_dramaturgy
concepts.definition: Erving Goffman. Self-presentation as theatrical performance. Front + back stage. 'Presentation of Self in Everyday Life' 1956.

concepts.name: bourdieu_habitus
concepts.definition: Pierre Bourdieu. Habitus = embodied dispositions acquired through socialisation. Field + capital + habitus shape practice.

concepts.name: bourdieu_cultural_capital
concepts.definition: Embodied + objectified + institutionalised. Economic, cultural, social, symbolic capitals. Mediates reproduction of inequality.

concepts.name: social_stratification
concepts.definition: Hierarchical arrangement of groups by power, wealth, status. Class, caste, race, gender systems. Substrate analogue: substrate's inequality structures.

concepts.name: social_mobility
concepts.definition: Movement between strata. Intergenerational vs intragenerational. Vertical vs horizontal.

concepts.name: intersectionality
concepts.definition: Kimberlé Crenshaw 1989. Race + gender + class etc. mutually constitute experience. Cannot reduce to single axis.

concepts.name: social_construction
concepts.definition: Berger + Luckmann 1966. Social phenomena (race, gender, money, nation) constructed through repeated collective action, not natural kinds. Substrate analogue: substrate's emergent shared categories.

concepts.name: social_reproduction
concepts.definition: How structures persist across generations. Family, education, culture transmit + reproduce inequalities.

concepts.name: agency_structure
concepts.definition: Classic debate. Individual agency vs structural constraints. Giddens's structuration: structures both constrain + enable.

concepts.name: social_network
concepts.definition: Pattern of ties between actors. Granovetter's strength of weak ties. Small world, scale-free properties.

concepts.name: weak_ties_strength
concepts.definition: Granovetter 1973. Weak ties bridge clusters → new information; strong ties within cluster → redundant.

concepts.name: social_capital
concepts.definition: Putnam. Networks + norms enabling cooperation. Bonding (within group) vs bridging (between groups).

concepts.name: collective_behavior
concepts.definition: Group action — crowds, social movements, fads, panics. Le Bon, Tarde, McAdam.

concepts.name: social_movement
concepts.definition: Sustained collective action seeking change. Resource mobilisation, political process, framing theories.

concepts.name: globalisation
concepts.definition: Increasing worldwide interconnection. Economic, cultural, political. Robertson, Castells, Sassen.

concepts.name: social_facts_durkheim
concepts.definition: Durkheim. External + coercive social phenomena (suicide rates, marriage rates) following own laws. Substrate analogue: substrate's emergent-pattern level.

rules.name: structure_constrains_agency
rules.head: Jabberwock examines social behavior
rules.body: individual agency operates within structural constraints (class, institutions, networks). Agency + structure mutually constitute (Giddens). Substrate's structure-enabled-and-constrained agency.

rules.name: social_facts_are_emergent_real
rules.head: Jabberwock considers a social phenomenon
rules.body: social facts (rates, institutions, norms) are external + coercive — real in their consequences regardless of individual beliefs. Durkheim. Substrate's emergent-pattern realism.

rules.name: stratification_reproduces_through_capital_transmission
rules.head: Jabberwock asks why inequality persists
rules.body: economic + cultural + social capital transmitted through family + education reproduces stratification across generations. Bourdieu. Substrate's inertial inequality.

rules.name: weak_ties_bridge_information
rules.head: Jabberwock seeks novel information through networks
rules.body: weak ties (acquaintances, bridges) carry new information across clusters; strong ties recycle within-cluster information. Granovetter 1973.

rules.name: self_emerges_through_symbolic_interaction
rules.head: Jabberwock considers identity formation
rules.body: self develops through interaction with others using shared symbols. Mead. Substrate's relational self-formation.
